There were no courts and no police, only the willingness of others to intervene. Losing every person who would speak for you was not an abstraction in that city. It was the definition of being finished.
studies.didYouKnow: The plural for intercessors occurs twice in the Quran and both times inside a sentence denying there are any. The ordinary word for a friend appears in this exact form once. And the word for the second chance being wished for is the one used of horsemen wheeling round to charge again, so the request is phrased as a return to the field.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Naming a friend alongside an advocate says something about what people are actually for. An intercessor is a mechanism; a friend is a relation, and the passage counts the loss of both. That treats human closeness as a real good rather than a distraction from God, which is why its absence can be named as part of the loss. The wish that follows asks for repetition, and the surah answers by moving to the next story.

crossReferences.why: Says close friends will be enemies to one another on that day, except the God-conscious.
Contains the only other use of the plural for intercessors, in a similar admission.
Records the same wish to be sent back, and says they would return to what they left.

studies.applyIt: Think of one person who would speak for you if you were not in the room, and do something small for them this week. A message, a favour, an hour. This passage counts a friend as a thing that can be lost, in the same breath as an advocate. Friendships are maintained or they are not, and nobody notices the maintenance until it stops.

studies.title: Their Brother Noah
studies.meaning: The refrain closes Abraham's account and the next one begins in the same breath. The people of Noah denied the messengers, in the plural, though only one came to them. Then a formula that will be repeated three more times in this surah with different names inserted: their brother said to them, will you not be wary? Noah's three sentences contain no theology. He states his relation to them, claims to be trustworthy, and asks for two things: wariness of God, and their attention.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan. Noah's account is the first of five that follow the same template: the people denied, a man of their own spoke, he claimed to be trustworthy, he asked for no payment, they refused, and the refrain closed the section. The commentators note that the word brother here means one of them by descent, not by faith, which is what makes the refusals a matter of a community rejecting its own. No occasion is reported.

keyTerms.note: Kinship by descent, not by belief. The phrase occurs four times in the Quran and all four are in this surah, introducing four of the prophets; the fifth is introduced without it.
From the root behind safety and faith, so the word means someone with whom a thing is safe. The phrase claiming it occurs five times in this surah, once in each account.
A verb for compliance with a person. It is paired every time with wariness of God, so obedience to the messenger is never asked for on its own account in these passages.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) had been known in Mecca as the trustworthy one before he said anything about revelation, and the Quraysh had used him to arbitrate. That reputation was a fact about him that his opponents could not withdraw. Hearing five earlier prophets each open by claiming exactly that word, an audience in Mecca was being told that the sequence had a place already prepared for the man in front of them.
studies.didYouKnow: The phrase naming a prophet as the people's own brother occurs four times in the Quran and every one is in this surah. The claim to be a trustworthy messenger occurs five times here and once elsewhere. Four of the five accounts open with a man of the people's own blood; the fifth prophet is introduced by name alone, without the word for brother.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The template itself is the argument. By running five prophets through the same six sentences, the surah makes the pattern visible in a way a single story could not: the message is constant, the resistance is constant, and the differences between the peoples turn out not to matter. It also grounds prophecy in kinship. The one sent is a brother, from inside the community, which removes any excuse that he could not understand them.

crossReferences.why: Opens the next account with the same words, replacing the name with that of another prophet.
Gives Noah's message in his own surah, with the same three requests in the same order.
Tells the same account at greater length, including the reply of Noah's people.

studies.applyIt: Notice how often you refuse advice because of who is giving it. A sibling, a colleague you have known too long, someone whose own life is untidy. Take one piece of advice you dismissed for that reason and consider it again on its own, for two minutes. These accounts turn on people refusing a brother, and the brother part is why.

studies.title: What Do I Know Of Them
studies.meaning: Noah repeats the disclaimer that will be repeated four more times in this surah, once by each of the prophets who follow: I ask you no payment. Then the objection, and it is about class. Shall we believe you when the lowest sort follow you? Noah's answer refuses the question twice over. He does not defend his followers, and he does not accept that their standing is his business. Their account is with my Lord, not with me.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan. The same objection was being made in Mecca, where the early community included slaves, freedmen and men without clan backing, and the leadership is reported to have asked that these be sent away before any conversation could happen. The commentators connect the two directly. Noah's reply, which declines to assess anybody's worth, is preserved in almost the same words in another surah. No occasion is reported for this passage.

keyTerms.note: A superlative for the most contemptible, applied to people by rank rather than by conduct. It occurs once in the Quran, and it is a word about who someone's parents were.
A word from arithmetic, the same one used for settling a debt. Placing the followers' accounts with God removes them from the prophet's ledger as well as from the objectors'.
A verb for noticing something by feel rather than by reasoning it out. Noah ends on the softer word, so the rebuke is that they have not registered the point rather than that they cannot follow it.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Rank in Mecca was visible in everything: where a man sat, whom he could marry, whether his testimony carried. Early converts included people at the bottom of that order, and the reports describe the leading men objecting to sitting alongside them. A message that arrived without asking about lineage was, for the people it reached first, the first thing in their lives that had not.
studies.didYouKnow: The word the objectors use for Noah's followers occurs once in the whole Quran. It is a superlative about social rank, not about behaviour, and Noah does not dispute it; he says he has no knowledge of what they do. The same disclaimer about payment that opens this passage appears five times in this surah, always in identical words.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Noah is offered an easy defence and declines it. He could have argued that his followers are better than they look, which would have accepted the premise that their worth was on trial. Instead he says he does not know what they do and that their reckoning is not his. That places the assessment of persons outside human competence altogether, including the prophet's. It also removes the only condition on which the objectors were willing to listen.

crossReferences.why: Gives the same objection about the lowly followers and Noah's refusal to drive them away.
Instructs that those who call on their Lord morning and evening are not to be dismissed.
Tells the listener to keep his eyes on such people rather than on those with wealth.

studies.applyIt: Notice whose opinion you weigh by their position rather than their point. The junior person in the meeting, the relative without a degree, the neighbour whose house is a mess. Take one thing said by someone in that category this week and consider it as if a person you respect had said it. Nothing more. Just run the sentence through the other filter.
